prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind farm O&M concept. Boundary: offshore generation assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external organizations; electrical boundary up to Grid Interface Relay (external grid interface). Out of scope: public grid beyond connection point; non-farm port operations. Turbine: Turbine Controller (alias Glassfin; per-turbine control function), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor (distinct for maintenance/condition review), Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone: blade assessment asset. Offshore Substation (alias Morrowick): offshore electrical collection/switching; contains Main Transformer; Export Cable Monitor (export system). SCADA Gateway: supervisory monitoring/control interface. Shore Control Room: shore operating location for authorized personnel; continuous monitoring, dispatch coordination; coordinates with Fleet Dispatch Console (resource coordination) and Maintenance Planning Engine (maintenance preparation/sequencing). Marine: Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, Helideck, vessel procedures. Workforce access: North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner, Personnel Tracking Console. Supply: Warehouse System, Spares Hub (inventory/replenishment). External: Weather Service (alias Pale Lantern; weather info), Metocean Buoy (offshore environmental observations), grid dispatch/operations, port support, suppliers, emergency response. Enabling functions in boundary: cybersecurity, communications, fire protection, backup power. Objectives: reliable generation, safety, asset integrity; availability via condition monitoring, fault response, planned maintenance, coordinated access. Requirements: work shall be authorized, hazards controlled, personnel and vessels accounted for; prevent pollution, minimize marine disturbance, respond promptly to environmental incidents. Modes: commissioning/acceptance (documented handover construction→operations control with verification); normal service (decisions on validated asset status, approved procedures, forecasts, grid instructions); planned maintenance (by condition, resources, access, production); unplanned maintenance (prioritized fault assessment, severity-based mobilization); major refurbishment; decommissioning (safe isolation, removal planning, transfer of residual records to responsible organization).

Document units:
S045: Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, and Service Operations Vessel represent marine resources that may support offshore work.
S046: Helideck is included as an access facility for activities supported by helicopter operations.
S047: Personnel Tracking Console represents the personnel location and accountability function.
S048: Warehouse System and Spares Hub represent the inventory and logistics context for maintenance materials.
S049: Work Permit Portal and Cybersecurity Gateway represent enabling functions that support controlled and secure operations.
S050: The operating concept also recognizes grid, emergency response, communications, and port support as external or enabling capabilities.
S051: The system architecture separates offshore equipment, operational services, and shore-based decision functions while preserving defined interfaces between them.
S052: The SCADA Gateway provides a controlled boundary for supervisory data exchange between offshore assets and shore-based operations.
S053: For this concept, SCADA Gateway is designated Juniper Vale as its operational alias.
S054: The Maintenance Planning Engine supports work preparation by organizing maintenance needs, resource considerations, and planning constraints.
S055: For this concept, Maintenance Planning Engine is designated Thistle Crown as its operational alias.
S056: The Shore Control Room is the principal shore-based setting for monitoring and coordinating wind farm operations.
S057: For this concept, Shore Control Room is designated Amber Quay as its operational alias.
S058: These three components have distinct responsibilities and are treated as cooperating parts of one operational system.
S059: The SCADA Gateway mediates supervisory exchanges and supports consistent access to operational information.
S060: The Turbine Controller performs local turbine control functions within the offshore equipment environment.
S061: The Turbine Controller produces the Pitch Deviation Notice for operational handling.
S062: The SCADA Engineer maintains the configuration and technical integrity of supervisory interfaces.
S063: The Control Engineer uses the shore-based operational picture to assess equipment status and coordinate response.
S064: The Shore Control Room provides a shared operational context for personnel responsible for offshore assets.
S065: The Duty Planner uses the Maintenance Planning Engine to prepare and review maintenance activities.
S066: The Maintenance Planning Engine supports planning decisions without replacing the judgment of the Duty Planner.
S067: The Weather Service contributes environmental information to operational planning and coordination.
S068: The Marine Coordinator considers offshore conditions and vessel availability when coordinating access to work sites.
S069: The Fleet Dispatch Console provides a fleet-level view of dispatch activity for operational coordination.
S070: The Work Permit Portal supports authorization processes that govern work under controlled conditions.
